1.name: Anime Jungle
1.status_note: Official site still lists the Little Tokyo store; no closure reports found. Not checked against a 2026 Google/Yelp listing.
1.address: 319 E 2nd St, Suite 103, Los Angeles, CA 90012
1.description: A large anime and hobby store inside the Little Tokyo Mall, also known as Entertainment Hobby Shop Jungle. It stocks figures, model kits, trading cards and other Japanese pop-culture merchandise, and has hosted brand pop-ups such as Bandai Hobby and Godzilla events.
1.owner_story: Run by Tetsu Shiota, an Osaka native whose family business started as a small anime shop in Osaka in 1996. After a 1999 survey of college anime club members picked Little Tokyo as the best spot for an anime store, the company opened here and later added more shops in the neighborhood.
1.parking_note: Official site says to park in the Little Tokyo Mall structure and take the elevator to the ground floor. Rates not confirmed.

2.name: Anzen Hardware
2.status_note: Closed at its longtime 309 E 1st St shop in 2023 (displaced amid a rent increase), then reopened at 220 E 1st St in late 2025 under the founding family. Hours below are from the Dec 2025 reopening article and may have changed.
2.description: A long-running Little Tokyo hardware store best known for Japanese kitchen knives, gardening tools and household goods. After nearly disappearing in 2023 it reopened nearby, open on weekends and by appointment on other days.
2.owner_story: Tsutomu Maehara founded the business in 1946 as Anzen Hotel Supply Co., supplying the small hotels and apartments that Japanese American owners ran after the war. The reopened store is back in the hands of his family, including his youngest child, Jo Ann Hirose.

3.name: Blooming Art Gallery
3.status_note: Listed among Little Tokyo Historical Society legacy businesses, but no address, hours or current listing could be found online.
3.description: A Little Tokyo art gallery recognized as a neighborhood legacy business. No reliable details about what it currently sells or shows were found, so check in person.

4.name: Bunkado
4.status_note: Listed as operating in Rafu Shimpo's Aug 2024 legacy business guide; no closure reports found. Hours are from an undated Time Out listing. Founding year given as 1946 by Rafu Shimpo; Time Out says 1945.
4.description: A family-run First Street shop selling traditional Japanese gifts and household items. Upstairs is an antiques and ceramics area with pottery, calligraphy pieces, vintage kimono and Japanese records.
4.owner_story: Bunkado has been on First Street since the 1940s and is now run by third-generation owner Irene Tsukada Simonian.

5.name: CRFT by Maki
5.status_note: Shop opened at 341 E 1st St in Jan 2020 and hosted an exhibit there in late 2023; no newer confirmation found.
5.description: A small shop for a Los Angeles lifestyle brand making simple, sporty clothing such as tees, hoodies and crewnecks marked with an origami crane logo. The brand also makes short films about Japanese American stories and the space has hosted community exhibits.
5.owner_story: Founder Darin Maki grew up in Montebello, played pro basketball in Japan, and launched the brand in January 2018. His mother taught him to sew, and his family has deep Little Tokyo ties: his great-grandmother ran a restaurant there and his grandmother worked at Umeya Rice Cake Co.

6.name: Hob Nob
6.status_note: Yelp listing updated May 2026 (not opened directly). Address given as 139 Japanese Village Plaza by Yelp and some directories, 141 by others. The old shophobnob.com domain now shows unrelated spam, so it is not listed as the website.
6.address: 139 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
6.description: A women's fashion and accessories boutique inside Japanese Village Plaza, selling trendy tops, dresses, bags and sunglasses. It began as a gift and souvenir shop before changing focus to apparel.
6.owner_story: Song Nam An established the business in 2000; it first operated as Giftime, a gift and souvenir shop, before becoming The Hob Nob Shop. It was featured by Metro in 2019 as a recipient of its Business Interruption Fund during rail construction.

7.name: Japangeles
7.status_note: Official site lists a flagship store with daily hours. One directory claims they are online-only; the official site contradicts that. A guide credits founder Roy Kuroyanagi (2009) but the official site says 'Est 2010' - founder detail not verified.
7.address: 141 Japanese Village Plaza, Los Angeles, CA 90012
7.description: The flagship shop of a local apparel brand that mixes Japanese and Southern California style. It sells tees, caps and other streetwear, including collaborations with Little Tokyo businesses.

8.name: Ginza USA
8.status_note: Appears in the Little Tokyo Historical Society legacy business images, but no current address, hours or official listing found. Described as being on E 1st St near Central Ave. A gift-card site names the owner as Yoshi Yamamoto; not verified, so not used.
8.description: A small First Street shop described by reviewers as selling Japanese gifts, books, music and collectibles, including records. Details could not be confirmed from an official source.

9.name: Little Tokyo Florist
9.status_note: Listed as operating in Rafu Shimpo's Aug 2024 legacy business guide; no closure reports found.
9.address: 333 S Alameda St, #110, Los Angeles, CA 90013
9.description: A florist in the Little Tokyo Galleria offering bouquets, ikebana arrangements and bonsai. It also runs occasional workshops announced on social media.
9.owner_story: Owned by Yuka Mizusawa; Rafu Shimpo describes the shop as rooted in Japanese American tradition.

10.name: Kinokuniya Book Store of America
10.status_note: The Weller Court store closed July 21, 2025. After a temporary shop at The Bloc downtown, Kinokuniya reopened in Little Tokyo in June 2026 in the Kajima Building (grand opening reception July 1, 2026), about twice the old size. Phone number comes from a search summary of a Rafu Shimpo listing; verify.
10.address: 101 S San Pedro St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
10.description: The Los Angeles branch of the Japanese bookstore chain, now in a larger space at First and San Pedro. It carries Japanese and English books, manga, magazines and stationery.

11.name: Make Asobi
11.status_note: Only passing mentions in older blog guides (as a Japanese cosmetics shop). One guide gives 141 Japanese Village Plaza, which conflicts with Japangeles' address, so no address is given.
11.description: A beauty shop mentioned in Little Tokyo guides for its Japanese cosmetics and bath products. Current details could not be confirmed.

12.name: Popkiller
12.status_note: Brand website is active (2026) and a guide says Little Tokyo is its last remaining store, but no 2024+ source confirms the storefront. Address and phone are from a 2013 Time Out listing; a sister shop, Pop Little Tokyo, was at 349 E 2nd St.
12.description: A quirky Second Street shop mixing vintage clothing with the brand's own Japanese- and LA-themed tees and accessories. It also carries toys, patches, records and novelty items.
12.owner_story: Founded by Ricky Takizawa; the shop celebrated its 13th anniversary in 2016. Popkiller once had four stores, and the Little Tokyo location is the one that remained.

13.name: Rafu Bussan
13.status_note: Moved from 326 E 2nd St to Honda Plaza around 2016. Listed in Rafu Shimpo's Aug 2024 guide, which asks visitors to give advance notice before coming by. A Time Out page marked 'CLOSED' appears to refer to an old listing.
13.description: A longtime importer of Japanese housewares and gifts, from fine tableware and china to kitchen appliances. It now operates from Honda Plaza on Second Street.
13.owner_story: Rafu Bussan opened in 1958 on First Street and moved to Second Street in 1978. Owner Aiko Kawaratani relocated the store to Honda Plaza in 2016.
13.parking_note: Rafu Shimpo notes parking at Honda Plaza as a convenience; rates not confirmed.

14.name: RIF LA
14.status_note: Listed in an Oct 2024 sneaker store guide; no closure reports found.
14.description: A consignment shop for sneakers and secondhand streetwear on Second Street. It is known for rare and limited sneakers and for streetwear sourced from buying trips to Japan.
14.owner_story: Jeff Malabanan and Ed Mateo opened RIF LA in Little Tokyo in 2006 after meeting while shopping at Supreme.

15.name: Utsuwa-No-Yakata
15.status_note: Listed as operating in Rafu Shimpo's Aug 2024 legacy guide. Hours are from a travel aggregator (Thatch) and may be outdated.
15.address: 333 S Alameda St, Ste 101, Los Angeles, CA 90013
15.description: A pottery shop on the ground floor of the Little Tokyo Galleria, focused mostly on handmade ceramics from Japan. Shelves hold plates, cups, bowls, vases and decor, and it often runs sales.

16.name: Shop Ashiya
16.status_note: The brief says it was reported closed in early 2024, but no source confirming the closure (or that it is open) was found. Only an older blog lists it as a women's clothing shop in Weller Court.
16.description: A Weller Court shop described in a blog as selling cute women's and girls' clothing. Its current status could not be confirmed.

17.name: Tokyo Japanese Outlet
17.status_note: Older guides place a shop by this name near Japanese Village Plaza; another listing puts it on Sawtelle Blvd. A Foursquare list shows 'Tokyo Japanese Lifestyle' at 114 Japanese Village Plaza, possibly the same chain but unconfirmed.
17.description: A gift and lifestyle shop described in guides as selling cute and unusual Japanese items such as plush toys, bento gear and incense. Location and status need checking.

18.name: Casa Heiwa / Little Tokyo Service Center
18.address: 231 E 3rd St, Suite G-106, Los Angeles, CA 90013
18.hours_note: LTSC office: Mon-Fri 9am-12pm and 1-4pm (closed for lunch). Casa Heiwa apartments are private residences.
18.description: Casa Heiwa is a mixed-use building with affordable apartments for seniors and families, and it houses the main office of the Little Tokyo Service Center. LTSC is a nonprofit that offers social services and builds affordable housing and community spaces in Little Tokyo and beyond.
18.history: LTSC was founded in 1979 by representatives of Japanese American groups as a multipurpose social service center; its community development arm later merged into the main organization. Casa Heiwa's opening year was not confirmed.

19.name: Centenary United Methodist Church
19.address: 300 S Central Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90013
19.hours_note: Sunday worship in person and online: 9:30am (Japanese) and 11am. Office hours not published.
19.description: A Japanese American United Methodist congregation at the corner of 3rd Street and Central Avenue. It holds Sunday services in Japanese and English and is one of the oldest Japanese American churches in Los Angeles.
19.history: Founded in June 1896 by Issei immigrants as the Japanese Methodist Episcopal Mission. Restrictive covenants pushed it out of Little Tokyo in the 1920s; it returned and held its first service in its current building on October 2, 1988.

20.name: Far East Lounge (now J-Town Senior Connection)
20.hours_note: A directory listing says hours vary with the class schedule. Current status not confirmed with LTSC.
20.description: A community lounge run by the Little Tokyo Service Center inside the historic Far East Building, used for classes and gatherings for seniors and neighbors. A directory listing says it has been renamed J-Town Senior Connection. It is separate from Far Bar, the bar next door at 347 E 1st St.
20.history: The Far East Building was home to the Far East Cafe, a Cantonese-American restaurant that opened in 1935 and was a long-time community gathering spot until the 1994 Northridge earthquake. The lounge held a grand opening program in 2014 (year of lounge opening not confirmed).

21.name: Go For Broke National Education Center & Go For Broke Monument
21.address: 355 E 1st St, Los Angeles, CA 90012 (organization address); Monument at 160 N Central Ave
21.hours_note: Hours shown are for the 'Defining Courage' exhibition. The Monument is free and open to the public during limited hours due to temporary construction (exact hours not published).
21.admission: Defining Courage exhibition: $10 general; $5 seniors 62+ and students with ID. Monument: free.
21.description: The Go For Broke Monument honors Japanese American soldiers of World War II and is engraved with the names of more than 16,000 who served. The nonprofit's 'Defining Courage' exhibition tells their story with oral histories and interactive stations.
21.history: The Monument was dedicated on June 5, 1999, next to the Japanese American National Museum. The education center moved from Torrance into JANM's historic building (the former Nishi Hongwanji temple) and opened its exhibition on May 28, 2016.

22.name: Higashi Honganji Buddhist Temple
22.hours_note: These are office hours from the temple website. Sunday morning services reported by secondary sources (Time Out: 10am); service time not confirmed on the official site. Phone number from secondary source.
22.description: A Jodo Shinshu Buddhist temple on 3rd Street that serves as the U.S. headquarters for the Higashi Honganji (Shinshu Otani-ha) tradition. Its main hall holds services in Japanese and English.
22.history: The congregation traces back to 1904, when it began as the Rafu Bukkyokai (Los Angeles Buddhist Mission). The present temple at 505 E 3rd St was dedicated in 1976.

23.name: Japanese American Cultural & Community Center (JACCC)
23.address: 244 S San Pedro St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
23.hours_note: Office hours. Aratani Theatre box office: Wed & Fri 11am-2pm, (213) 680-3700. James Irvine Japanese Garden hours not published on JACCC site (secondary sources say Tue-Fri 10am-5pm, unverified).
23.admission: Free to visit; theater events ticketed
23.description: A major Japanese American arts and community center with offices, the Aratani Theatre, and a large public plaza on San Pedro Street. Below the plaza is the James Irvine Japanese Garden, a quiet stream garden designed by landscape architect Takeo Uesugi.
23.history: The organization was founded in 1971 and its center building opened in 1980; the garden was also completed in 1980 for the centennial of Japanese in the U.S. The Japan America Theatre (now Aratani Theatre) opened in April 1983.

24.name: Japanese American National Museum (JANM)
24.address: 100 N Central Ave, Los Angeles, CA 90012
24.hours_note: TEMPORARILY CLOSED: the JANM Pavilion is closed for renovation and reopens January 23, 2027. From reopening: Tue-Sun 11am-5pm, Fri until 8pm, closed Mon. Status set to 'unknown' because the schema has no 'temporarily closed' value.
24.admission: From Jan 23, 2027: adults $20, seniors 62+ $15, college students & youth 6-18 $12, 5 and under free, members free; free Fridays after 5pm and every 1st Friday.
24.description: The largest museum in the U.S. dedicated to Japanese American history, art and culture, including the WWII incarceration. Its modern pavilion faces the historic former Nishi Hongwanji temple building across the plaza.
24.history: JANM opened to the public in 1992 in the restored 1925 Nishi Hongwanji Buddhist Temple building. The Pavilion is currently being renovated.

25.name: Jodoshu Buddhist Temple (former Little Tokyo site)
25.hours_note: Jodo Shu North America left the Little Tokyo building after March 2023; services are now held at Torrance Cultural Arts Center while it seeks a new site. Phone is the Torrance office.
25.description: This was the Little Tokyo home of Jodo Shu North America, a Pure Land Buddhist temple. The congregation moved out in 2023, citing safety concerns, and now meets in Torrance.
25.history: The temple moved to 442 E 3rd St with support from Bukkyo University, with a dedication in June 1992. It left the building after its Spring Higan service in March 2023.

26.name: Koyasan Buddhist Temple
26.hours_note: Visiting/office hours not published. Holds classes (e.g. taiko Mondays 6-7:30pm, monthly yoga & sound bath) and special services; call ahead.
26.description: A Shingon Buddhist temple set back from 1st Street behind a gate, in the middle of Little Tokyo's historic block. It hosts services, taiko, chanting and calligraphy classes.
known_for: Oldest Shingon temple in the U.S.
26.history: Founded in 1912 in a Little Tokyo storefront as the first Shingon temple in the United States. Its current 1st Street building dates to about 1939-1940, and during WWII it sheltered Japanese Americans removed from Terminal Island.

27.name: Little Tokyo Branch Library (LAPL)
27.address: 203 S Los Angeles St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
27.hours_note: Free valet parking at the STOA Apartments entrance next door (no tip required).
27.description: A Los Angeles Public Library branch whose building was designed to reflect traditional Japanese architecture, with three interior gardens. It offers free Wi-Fi, computers and library services in the heart of Little Tokyo.
27.history: Library service began with a bookmobile stop in 1977 and a branch opened in 1989 in space donated by Centenary UMC. The current 12,500 sq ft building opened on September 8, 2005.

28.name: Little Tokyo Towers
28.hours_note: Private residential building; not open to visitors.
28.description: A high-rise apartment building providing affordable housing for seniors 62 and over, built by Little Tokyo community organizations. It is one of the tallest buildings in Little Tokyo and a residential anchor for elderly residents.
28.history: Built in 1975 with a HUD loan and sponsorship by Japanese American nonprofits; it has about 301 units. A renovation secured 55 more years of affordability, and a rededication was held October 26, 2024.

29.name: St. Francis Xavier Chapel Japanese Catholic Center
29.address: 222 S Hewitt St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
29.hours_note: Office hours Mon-Fri 9am-5pm (closed 12:30-1:30). Mass: Sat 5pm (English vigil); Sun 8:30am (Japanese) and 10am (English); weekday 12:05pm Mon, Wed, Thu, Fri (may change). Weekend office hours not published (shown as closed).
29.description: A Japanese Catholic chapel and community center on Hewitt Street, formerly known as Maryknoll. It holds Masses in Japanese and English and describes itself as the last remaining Japanese Catholic Center in the U.S.
29.history: A Japanese Catholic mission on Hewitt Street was dedicated in 1912 under the patronage of St. Francis Xavier. The center was later known as Maryknoll and has since returned to the St. Francis Xavier name.

30.name: Nishi Hongwanji Los Angeles Betsuin
30.hours_note: Office hours (may vary on major holidays). Services start at 10am with Dharma discussion after (day of week not stated on homepage; typically Sunday — unverified).
30.description: A large Jodo Shinshu Buddhist temple on the east end of 1st Street. It is the Los Angeles 'betsuin' (regional head temple) of the Hongwanji tradition.
known_for: Original 1925 temple now part of JANM
30.history: Founded in 1905. Its 1925 temple at 1st St & Central Ave later became the home of JANM; the congregation moved to its current site at 815 E 1st St in 1969.

31.name: Ten Terraces Parking Garage
31.hours_note: Could not confirm an address or operator for a garage by this name. Possibly the '420 E 3rd St Garage' (entrance on Boyd St) on the Little Tokyo Community Council parking map — unverified match.
31.description: Garage shown on the official visitor map; likely the 420 E 3rd St garage with its entrance on Boyd St (not yet confirmed).

park.rates_text: No rates found. Could not confirm the 'Ten Terraces' name. A Parkopedia listing exists for a 'Little Tokyo Associates' garage at 425 Boyd St (blocked; may or may not be the same).
park.entrance: Boyd St (Go Little Tokyo map: 'Parking Lot Entrance on Boyd St')

32.name: Union Center for the Arts
32.address: 120 Judge John Aiso St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
32.hours_note: Hours vary by event. Tuesday Night Cafe (free open mic/performance series) has traditionally run 1st & 3rd Tuesdays, April-October, 7:30pm in the Aratani Courtyard — check tuesdaynightproject.org for current dates.
32.admission: Varies by event; Tuesday Night Cafe is free
32.description: The restored former Japanese Union Church, now an arts hub. It houses East West Players' David Henry Hwang Theater, the media arts group Visual Communications, and LA Artcore, and hosts the long-running Tuesday Night Cafe.
known_for: East West Players (David Henry Hwang Theater)
32.history: Built in 1923 as the Japanese Union Church for three Japanese American congregations; during WWII it was a departure point for removal to Manzanar. Little Tokyo Service Center renovated it, and East West Players moved in in 1998.

33.name: Union Church of Los Angeles
33.hours_note: Sunday worship: 9am (Japanese) and 11am (English). Office hours not published.
33.description: A Japanese American Protestant congregation holding Sunday services in Japanese and English at 3rd and San Pedro Streets. It is the continuation of the congregation that built the original Union Church, now the Union Center for the Arts.
33.history: The congregation worshipped in the 1923 Union Church building on what is now Judge John Aiso St until the 1970s, when it moved to its current location at 3rd and San Pedro. Founding year of the congregation not confirmed.

34.name: Wakaba Parking Garage
34.hours_note: Garage beneath the Wakaba apartments; JANM lists 232 E 2nd St as a Joe's Auto Parks location. Rates/hours not confirmed from operator.
34.description: A public parking garage in the Wakaba apartment building on 2nd Street, at the west side of Little Tokyo. Listed by JANM among nearby parking options.

park.rates_text: No posted drive-up rates found. SpotHero facility page: from $15; SpotHero Little Tokyo page: 'Starting at $10'.
park.entrance: South side of E 2nd St between San Pedro St and S Los Angeles St (SpotHero). Height limit 8'2".

35.name: Zenshuji Soto Mission
35.address: 123 S Hewitt St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
35.hours_note: Visiting hours not published. Active 2026 calendar: monthly services (e.g. Nov 15 monthly service & rakugo), Rohatsu sesshin Nov 29-Dec 5, temple closed Dec 7 and Jan 2-4. Address/phone from secondary sources.
35.description: A Soto Zen Buddhist temple on Hewitt Street offering zazen practice, monthly services and seasonal ceremonies in a Japanese-style setting. It is regarded as the first Soto Zen temple in North America.
known_for: First Soto Zen temple in North America
35.history: Established in 1922 by Rev. Hosen Isobe. Taizan Maezumi served as a priest here from 1956 to 1966 before founding Zen Center of Los Angeles.

36.name: Aloha Cafe
36.status_note: Official site says the dining room is temporarily closed; take-out and catering only. Site lists only Thu-Fri hours, so other days are unconfirmed.
36.address: 410 E 2nd St, Los Angeles, CA 90012 (Honda Plaza)
36.description: A small Hawaiian-style cafe in Honda Plaza serving island comfort food such as plate lunches and rice bowls. Right now it runs as a take-out and catering kitchen rather than a sit-down spot.
36.owner_story: The cafe traces back to Maui-born chef Komai, who started an Aloha Cafe in Monterey Park in the mid-1990s. Jennifer Lee, who learned from him, revived it with him in Monterey Park (2004-2007) and later moved it to Little Tokyo; she now runs it with her brother Kenneth Lee.
36.parking_note: Honda Plaza has a small shared lot (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source).

37.name: Azay
37.status_note: Closed after an April 1, 2025 fire and water damage; reopened December 2025. Dinner service is on pause.
37.description: A daytime restaurant on First Street that blends French technique with Japanese home cooking. Its traditional Japanese breakfast set is the most popular order, alongside a lunch menu; last orders are taken at 1:45 pm.
37.owner_story: Azay was opened in 2019 by Kyoto-born chef Akira Hirose, who trained in France and earlier ran Maison Akira in Pasadena. After he died in September 2024, his son Philip Hirose took over the restaurant, and his mother Jo Ann Hirose also works there.
37.parking_note: Official site points to the Aiso parking garage across the street, plus metered street parking.

38.name: Cafe Dulce
38.status_note: Owner's chain had five locations as of Oct 2025 (USC News); Little Tokyo hours come from an aggregator refreshed Nov 2026, not the cafe itself. Official site could not be loaded.
38.address: 134 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
38.description: A corner coffee bar and bakery at the Second Street end of Japanese Village Plaza. It pairs espresso drinks and teas with creative pastries and doughnuts, plus sandwiches and salads.
38.owner_story: Laura Choi planned the bakery, and her son James Choi left his auditing job at Ernst & Young to run it when her baking partner quit just before opening. Laura died in 2013; James has since grown Cafe Dulce to several LA locations.
38.parking_note: Japanese Village Plaza has a paid parking lot (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source).

39.name: Donatsu
39.status_note: Listed as closed on Yelp; reported closed around March 2022.
39.address: 330 E 2nd St, Suite C, Los Angeles, CA 90012
39.description: A small shop across from Japanese Village Plaza making fully vegan doughnuts, many in Japanese-inspired flavors. It also serves coffee drinks and teas.
39.owner_story: The shop is run by married owners Jenny and Nite Ban and opened in January 2019.

40.name: Rakkan Ramen
40.description: The Little Tokyo branch of a Japanese ramen chain whose broths are built mainly on plant ingredients like kombu and mushrooms rather than pork bones. It serves late into the night, with vegan bowls and a patio open until 10 pm.

41.name: Far Bar
41.status_note: Official website is live; hours not published on the pages checked.
41.description: A bar tucked into the historic Far East Building, reached through an alley-style entrance. It is known for a deep list of Japanese beers and whiskies plus Asian-influenced bar food.
41.owner_story: The space was home to the Far East Cafe, a Cantonese chop suey restaurant dating to 1935, which let families eat free or pay later after World War II. It was condemned after the 1994 Northridge earthquake, restored with community help, and Far Bar opened in the building in the mid-2000s. (1935 refers to the Far East Cafe, not Far Bar itself.)

42.name: Fugetsu-Do
42.description: A family sweet shop making traditional Japanese mochi and manju by hand, including seasonal varieties sold only at the store. Its packaged sweets also reach Japanese markets on the West Coast.
42.owner_story: Founded in Little Tokyo in 1903, Fugetsu-Do is still family-owned. Master confectioner Brian Kito is the third-generation owner.

43.name: JiST Cafe
43.status_note: Closed at the end of May 2024 (Rafu Shimpo, June 2024).
43.address: 116 Judge John Aiso St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
43.description: A breakfast and lunch spot next to East West Players that mixes Japanese flavors into American brunch dishes. Diners come for hearty plates like pork-belly hash and omurice.
43.owner_story: JiST is run by chef Glen Ishii, a third-generation Little Tokyo local, with business partner Caroline Shin. Its roots go back to Tokyo Cafe, a family restaurant started by Ishii's grandmother (sources disagree on the year).

44.name: Hana Ichimonme
44.status_note: Yelp shows it open with current hours, closed Tuesdays (Nov 2026).
44.address: 333 S Alameda St, 3rd floor, Los Angeles, CA 90013 (Little Tokyo Galleria)
44.description: A long-running casual noodle restaurant on the top floor of the Little Tokyo Galleria, with plastic food models and origami in its window. It serves ramen and other homestyle Japanese dishes.
44.parking_note: The Galleria/mall building has its own parking (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source). Phone number is from an older aggregator (Allmenus) and is unverified.

45.name: Korea BBQ House
45.address: 123 Astronaut E S Onizuka St #302, Los Angeles, CA 90012 (Weller Court, 3rd floor)
45.description: A casual Korean restaurant on the top floor of Weller Court serving grilled meats and classic Korean plates. It is popular for its lunch specials, such as marinated short ribs.
45.parking_note: Weller Court has a parking structure (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source). Legacy status inferred from a 'Korea BBQ' logo on the LTHS legacy page.

46.name: Kouraku
46.status_note: Honored by the City of LA in Jan 2025. Rafu says it stays open until midnight (2 am Fri-Sat), but opening times were not confirmed, so hours are left null.
46.description: A late-night Little Tokyo diner serving homestyle Japanese dishes, best known for ramen with chashu pork. Recognized by the city as the oldest continually operating ramen restaurant in the U.S.
46.owner_story: Kouraku opened in 1976. Hiroshi Yamauchi took it over in 1986 and ran it until his death in 2020; Mamoru Tokuda is the current owner.

47.name: Sushi Gala
47.status_note: Now called Sushi Gala: same address and phone number (Yelp, Oct 2026).
47.address: 103 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
47.description: A casual Japanese Village Plaza eatery that began as a burger and sandwich counter and later added Japanese dishes. Its menu now spans ramen, teriyaki bowls, bento and sushi.
47.owner_story: According to the restaurant's own listing description, it started roughly 40 years ago serving burgers and sandwiches and added Japanese dishes over time at customers' request.
47.parking_note: Japanese Village Plaza has a paid parking lot (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source).

48.name: Little Tokyo Ice Cream & Yogurt
48.status_note: Only one thin directory listing found; no official site, hours or recent reviews.
48.address: 133 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
48.description: A small dessert counter in Japanese Village Plaza selling ice cream, mochi ice cream and frozen yogurt. It also offers milkshakes and drinks like Thai iced tea.
48.parking_note: Japanese Village Plaza has a paid parking lot (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source).

49.name: Sushi Takeda
49.status_note: Formerly named Sushi Hide. Reservations via Tock.
49.address: 123 Astronaut Ellison S. Onizuka St, Ste 307, Los Angeles, CA 90012 (Weller Court, 3rd floor)
49.description: A tiny Edomae-style omakase counter where chef Hide Takeda serves fish flown in from Tokyo's Toyosu market. Dinner adds seasonal cooked courses to the nigiri, while lunch is a lower-priced omakase (about $110-120 per Resy, Oct 2026; dinner about $300).
49.owner_story: Chef-owner Hideyuki 'Hide' Takeda previously worked at Sushi Tsujita on Sawtelle before running this counter, first as Sushi Hide and now under his own name.
49.parking_note: Weller Court has a parking structure (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source).

50.name: Mitsuru Cafe
50.status_note: Listed as active in Rafu's Aug 2024 legacy list. Not the same as Mitsuru Sushi & Grill, which closed Aug 31, 2025. Hours conflict between sources, so left null.
50.address: 117 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
50.description: A long-running walk-up stand in Japanese Village Plaza where you can watch red bean cakes being griddled in the window. It also sells festival-style snacks like dango and takoyaki.
50.parking_note: Japanese Village Plaza has a paid parking lot (general knowledge, not confirmed by a cited source). Rafu lists the address as 17 JVP Mall; Time Out and Franki say 117.

51.name: Mitsuru Sushi & Grill
51.status_note: Closed late August 2025 when the owners retired; the Rafu Shimpo gave Aug. 28, 2025 as the closing date and the Pacific Citizen reported Aug. 31. The business was sold to Little Akihabara Holdings, which planned a J-Pop culture cafe on First Street.
51.description: A long-running, diner-style Little Tokyo spot that mixed a front sushi bar with Japanese, Okinawan and American comfort food. It was also a regular meeting place for community groups.
known_for: Gacha plate with chashu and Portuguese sausage
51.owner_story: Mamoru and Dora Hanamure ran the restaurant for about 49 years. It began next to Kyodo Drug Store and grew into a full restaurant after the drugstore closed. During the pandemic it made bentos for seniors delivered through the Little Tokyo Service Center.

52.name: Mr. Ramen
52.status_note: Its official website lists current hours. Some third-party listings give slightly different hours.
52.description: A small, late-night ramen counter on First Street with a long menu of ramen styles, combos and a separate vegetarian menu. Customers draw on napkins, and the shop collects and shares the drawings.
52.owner_story: Mr. Ramen was founded in 1993 by a man the shop calls Shinobu-san. After he died in 2020, his sons took over the shop.
52.parking_note: No parking information was found. This is a First Street storefront, so assume street or garage parking.

53.name: Oomasa Restaurant
53.status_note: Rafu Shimpo featured it as an operating legacy business in Aug 2024, and listings show 2024-2025 reviews. No official website was found (the domain oomasala.com does not resolve), so hours are unconfirmed.
53.address: 100 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
53.description: A traditional sushi bar and Japanese restaurant by the tower entrance of Japanese Village Plaza. The menu covers sushi and sashimi plus teriyaki, tempura and combination plates.
53.parking_note: Japanese Village Plaza has its own paid parking lot. Validation for this restaurant is not verified.

54.name: Orochon Ramen
54.status_note: Hours are from the official website. A third-party listing shows later closing times, so they may have changed.
54.address: 123 Astronaut E S Onizuka St, Ste 303, Los Angeles, CA 90012
54.description: A ramen shop on the third floor of Weller Court, best known for very spicy bowls. It also serves miso ramen and simple teriyaki plates.
54.parking_note: A Wanderlog listing says Weller Court offers validated parking (not confirmed with the restaurant).

55.name: Rice & Nori
55.status_note: No closure reports were found, but I found no dated 2026 confirmation. Third-party listings show 11:00-21:00 daily, which is unverified. Phone numbers differ between listings: (213) 628-3114 and (213) 628-3111.
55.address: 123 Astronaut E S Onizuka St, Ste 103, Los Angeles, CA 90012
55.description: A tiny counter on the ground floor of Weller Court making triangle rice balls with many fillings, plus hand rolls and house pickles. Hand rolls are best eaten on the spot, since they soften when taken to go.
55.parking_note: Located in Weller Court, which has a parking structure. Validation for this shop is not verified.

56.name: Shabu Shabu House
56.status_note: Closed in October 2023 after 32 years when its Japanese Village Plaza lease ended and demolition of the space began. No reopening has been reported as of Nov 2026.
56.address: 127 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
56.description: A small counter restaurant where diners cooked thin slices of beef and vegetables in their own pot of broth, with ponzu and sesame dipping sauces. It is often cited as the first shabu-shabu restaurant in the United States.
known_for: First shabu-shabu restaurant in the U.S.
56.owner_story: Opened in 1991 by Yoshinobu Maruyama, who ran it with Masako Maruyama. They announced the closure only after it happened.
56.parking_note: It was in Japanese Village Plaza. The business is now closed.

57.name: Pasta e Pasta by Allegro
57.status_note: The Infatuation reviewed it on July 31, 2026. A third-party listing shows Monday closed, with lunch 11:30-14:00 and dinner from 17:00 the other days. These hours are unverified.
57.description: A Japanese-Italian spot serving thin spaghetti in many sauces, including tomato, cream, garlic oil and Japanese-style soy and seafood flavors. It is a branch of a Japan-founded Allegro restaurant group, with sister locations in Torrance and Cerritos.

58.name: Sushi & Teri
58.status_note: Online ordering and listings are active, but there are no official hours. A third-party listing shows 11:00-22:00 (Fri-Sat until 23:00), which is unverified.
58.address: 116 Japanese Village Plaza Mall, Los Angeles, CA 90012
58.description: A casual Japanese Village Plaza restaurant serving sushi, sashimi and rolls alongside teriyaki plates. Reviewers mention generous portions.
58.parking_note: Japanese Village Plaza has its own paid parking lot. Validation is not verified.

59.name: Sushi Komasa
59.status_note: Listed as permanently closed on Yelp and Foursquare.
59.description: A small, dinner-focused sushi bar next to the Japanese American National Museum, known in the 2000s-2010s for fresh fish at fair prices. Diners waiting for a seat marked their orders on a paper menu.

60.name: Sushi Gen
60.status_note: Open, but hours conflict across sources. Its website currently shows only 'Updating website'. Most sources agree on Monday closed and lunch about 11:00-14:00, but dinner days and times vary. The founding year is 1980 per the Consulate General of Japan and 1981 per Rafu Shimpo and FoodGPS.
60.description: One of Little Tokyo's best-known traditional sushi bars, praised for market-fresh fish at fairly moderate prices. Lines to sit at the sushi counter are common, and the lunchtime sashimi set is a favorite.
60.owner_story: Owner Toshiaki Toyoshima trained as a sushi chef in Tokyo from 1962 and came to the U.S. in 1973. He worked at a local Japanese restaurant before opening Sushi Gen. In 2019 Japan honored him with a ministerial award for promoting Japanese food overseas.

61.name: Tamon
61.status_note: 2025-2026 hotel listings say the Miyako Hotel serves breakfast at Tamon, but I found no current official hours. An older Gayot listing says lunch and dinner Mon, Tue and Thu-Sat. Discover LA lists the website tamon-ten.com, which I did not verify. The phone below is from Discover LA and may be the hotel's main line; Gayot lists 213-617-7839.
61.address: 328 E 1st St, 2nd floor (Miyako Hotel), Los Angeles, CA 90012
61.description: The Japanese restaurant inside the Miyako Hotel, serving sushi and other Japanese dishes, with a breakfast service for hotel guests. It sits next to the hotel's Ohjah Lounge bar and offers Japanese draft beer, sake and shochu.
61.parking_note: It is inside the Miyako Hotel. Hotel parking terms are not verified.

62.name: TaNoTa Takoyaki
62.status_note: No closure reports were found. I found no official hours: the website's store-info section is empty, and third-party hours conflict.
62.description: An Osaka-style takoyaki shop selling octopus-filled batter balls with a crisp shell and soft center, in flavors from classic sauce to ponzu and parmesan truffle. It shares its space and teppan grills with the okonomiyaki restaurant Chinchikurin.
62.owner_story: Osaka-born owner Takeo Shibatani started the business with two surfing friends, and the name comes from their initials. It ran as a food truck from 2010 before opening this storefront in March 2018. The company also wholesales frozen takoyaki to restaurants.

63.name: Tea Master
63.status_note: The online shop is active (it sells 2026 shincha). A third-party listing shows Monday closed, Tue-Thu and Sun 12:00-17:00, and Fri-Sat 12:00-20:00, but another listing differs, so treat these hours as unverified.
63.address: 450 E 2nd St, 2nd floor, Los Angeles, CA 90012
63.description: A second-floor matcha cafe and tea shop serving green tea drinks, lattes, smoothies and matcha soft serve. It also sells loose-leaf tea, matcha powder and teaware.
63.parking_note: Reviewers say parking nearby can be difficult.

64.name: Teishokuya of Tokyo (T.O.T.)
64.status_note: Featured as an operating legacy business in Aug 2024, with Yelp reviews as recent as Oct 2025. Its old website domain has lapsed and MapQuest shows it as 'Closed', so confirm status. Hours conflict: the Downtown LA directory says daily 11:30-22:30, while another listing shows Mon-Tue closed.
64.description: A casual restaurant serving Japanese set meals and comfort food: donburi, udon and soba, tempura, grilled fish and sushi. It also pours a wide range of sake.
64.owner_story: Rafu Shimpo notes that T.O.T. was part of Kagura Downtown, a former legacy business that has since closed.

65.name: Keepers
65.status_note: Yelp's listing is titled 'KEEPERS - CLOSED' (updated April 2026), and its sister spot Keepers Coffee is also marked closed (updated October 2026). Its website onlykeepers.co no longer resolves. I found no news article confirming the closure date.
65.address: 200 S Los Angeles St, Los Angeles, CA 90012
65.description: A restaurant and bar at the western edge of Little Tokyo that served New American brunch and dinner. It also ran a small coffee offshoot, Keepers Coffee.

66.name: Zencu Sushi & Grill
66.status_note: Delivery and listing pages are active, with reviews into 2025, but I found no 2026 confirmation. Its official domain zencu.com is now a parked for-sale page. Hours are from the Downtown LA directory (undated); another listing shows earlier closing times.
66.address: 319 E 2nd St, Ste 206, Los Angeles, CA 90012
66.description: An upstairs restaurant in the Little Tokyo Mall serving sushi and sashimi, creative rolls, bento boxes, tempura and noodles, with sake and beer. It has a sushi bar plus a private upper-floor space for large groups.
66.parking_note: The Downtown LA directory says the Little Tokyo Mall has parking. Validation terms are not verified.

metro.name: Little Tokyo/Arts District Station (Metro A & E Lines)
metro.address: 402 E 1st St, Los Angeles, CA 90012 (1st St & Central Ave)
metro.hours_note: Underground station at 1st St & Central Ave, across from JANM. Detailed entrance layout and service hours not confirmed; check metro.net.
metro.description: An underground light rail station serving the A Line and E Line, right at the edge of Little Tokyo across from JANM. The B/D Line subway is a few blocks away at Civic Center, and DASH A plus several Metro bus lines serve 1st Street.
known_for: E Line (to Santa Monica / East LA)
metro.history: Opened June 16, 2023 as part of the Regional Connector tunnel, replacing the earlier above-ground Gold Line station of the same name. The old L Line was split between the A and E lines at that time.
